findings: The repair avoids a silent loop-recovery carve-out by adding explicit advisory score-card status and activation requirements.
Retired milestone vocabulary and stale lower-numbered ADR references are removed from the #136 write scope.
Portfolio hyperscaler and industry-pattern rows are inventory only until validators, fixture-tree tests, workflows, and branch protection land.
Workflow Studio golden-signal work remains visible as a priority backlog item without claiming enforcement.
Advisory score-card rows now fail validation if they omit planned_verification_ref or activation_requires.
Ontology product edges are tested so Connect integration edges cannot point at missing product nodes.
Reviewers can distinguish active pre-push score cards from advisory portfolio inventory by reading enforcement_status.
Connect product graph nodes are consolidated under specs/products/ontology.json instead of the retired semantic registry path.
Targeted unit, integration, product-PRD, milestone-audit, retired-vocabulary, ADR-citation, and loop-recovery gates passed.
Loop recovery reports 14 score cards but still only executes 3 active commands, proving advisory rows are not silently run or silently skipped.

alternatives_named: Make portfolio score cards active immediately
Reintroduce the retired semantic registry path
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Use explicit advisory status with activation requirements and keep semantic product graph data in the active ontology spec.
rejected_reasons: Active rows would overclaim validators that do not exist.
The semantic registry path is retired by ADR-0130.

findings: No secrets or tenant data are touched.
The main safety concern is false assurance; advisory status prevents planned controls from being mistaken for active gates.
